cells.tense: The grip has already loosened and what came in behind it is yours to use — here, with your hand still on it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're already carrying well and take it one step past your usual stopping point — a call made, a draft sent — then notice which direction the momentum points.
cells.core:
You've let go of enough that the pictures in your head can be lived instead of rehearsed. Nothing has to be forced into focus; you take the step that's lit and the rest of the road shows up when you get there. That's not luck. Letting go and seeing clearly are the same motion, and you're in it.

What that looks like from outside: you'll say yes to something before the whole plan is drawn, and it will turn out fine. So test the edge of it. One call, one draft, one conversation — carry it a step further than you normally would, and let the answer tell you where the next step lands.
cells.sheetLine: You release on purpose, and what opens up gets used.
cells.verb: moving forward with only the next step lit, letting the shape of things arrive without forcing it into view
cells.place: the open hand — where what is no longer needed is set down on purpose so the held space can fill with what comes

cells.tense: You're bracing for a version of this that hasn't happened, and when it gets written, the words won't be the ones you rehearsed.
cells.ask: Name out loud or on paper what the dream is costing you right now — one true line about the life it's taking from — and then let one thing go unmanaged for today.
cells.core:
The picture stays a guest in the house — you can see a future and still live the afternoon you're in, and the picture gets sharper as you walk rather than standing in for the walking. That's what a clear eye looks like on an ordinary Tuesday: you set something down because it's done, and the next thing finds you.

What's running now is that the future version has taken over the present one. Every move gets rehearsed against a day that hasn't arrived, and the rehearsing feels like doing something. It isn't — the dream is eating the day it was supposed to serve. Try putting one true cost of it into words, and leave one detail of the day unmanaged. Something in your hands gets lighter when you set it down.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that closed, explaining why the room still matters.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you've let go of in the last year — a role, a plan, a version of yourself — and one glimmer of direction you noticed but explained away. Read them together.
cells.core:
Walking into a room without knowing yet how it goes is a thing you can do — the sense of direction shows up while you're standing in it, not before, and the body stays calm. You trust the step and the light arrives with it.

What's running now is narrower. Only what can be measured gets a vote, only what can be argued gets said, and the pull toward something gets filed as noise before it's given a hearing. The vision isn't gone — it's just stopped being allowed to matter. Putting the pull on paper isn't a vote for it; it's making sure it's on the table at all. What you pay attention to grows, and this has gone unattended.

cells.tense: You're inside a picture of your life you didn't admit you were painting, and the paint is still wet.
cells.ask: Sit somewhere quiet for ten minutes with no goal, and write three lines beginning 'the life being built here is…'. Leave them unedited, no plans, just what shows up.
cells.core:
You can name the life you're reaching for out loud — to yourself first — and set it beside the one you're living, and notice where they've drifted. That check is what keeps the picture yours instead of something you're following. Done regularly it takes ten minutes and it changes what you reach for next week.

What's happening now is the check isn't running. Week to week something is shaping the choices — what you reach for, what you let go of, what you call realistic — and none of it has been said out loud, even to you. Making it visible is the whole move. Then you can revise it. What shows up on the page was steering already.

attempts.check: The draft risks two unsupported claims: that the person once performed a release that went badly (Too Little's 'somewhere back there'), and that they have rejected a specific intuition (spiritual literalism is on the record, but its cost is not); both would need the reader to supply a story the record does not carry, so I have kept the location and dropped the history. A reader might reasonably say 'the dream I am living inside is already faithful' about Too Much, or 'what looks like flatness is grief I am carrying deliberately' — the cells must let that stand without arguing. The ask survives being wrong: naming what the dream is costing and changing one daily act teaches the person something either way, and a small marker for what's been released is useful whether or not the release was the point. The sentence that serves the writer more than the reader would be any line about the person 'already writing this life' — a good sound that names no act; cut it.
